Rachel —

We started seeing intermittent failures to our on-prem telemetry gateway around 07:40 PDT. Symptoms look like short-lived TCP resets and a subset of flows failing when the request takes a return path via the partner transit (hairpin). From the customer side we see requests reach the edge, but the response sometimes is not accepted by the initiator and the session drops. It feels like asymmetric routing plus port/sketchy SG state.

Attached is a tcpdump from our edge appliance showing repeated SYN/SYN-ACK but then RSTs after ~1s for some flows. Happy to hop on a quick triage call.

—Mike

Forwarding Mike's dump. Immediate observations after a quick look:
- Multiple flows show SYN->SYN/ACK delivered to remote edge, but subsequent packets (server->client) take a different exit interface (peer transit) and arrive with a different source path. That explains why client firewall drops the packet (no matching conntrack / expected ephemeral port mapping).
- We also see TCP MSS options intact; MTU doesn't look to be the first-order cause.
- Edge SNAT table shows ephemeral port reuse policy that can conflict with hairpinned return path when the partner rewrites source.

Action plan:
1) Rishi to validate conntrack behavior and whether our edge accepts replies from alternate upstreams when no symmetric NAT mapping exists.
2) Rachel to request sg-rules snapshot from Kestrel and confirm whether they SNAT to a single public IP.
3) Temporary mitigation: add a route policy to prefer symmetric return via our peering for the affected prefixes until we have a permanent fix.

Jonas

Quick lab reproduce and notes:
- I replayed a subset of the pcap in a controlled environment. When return traffic arrives from an unexpected next-hop (different source MAC / AS path), conntrack on our edge does not match the packet to the established tuple and treats it as NEW -> RST (or DROP depending on policy).
- Our edge config has strict "conntrack-strict" enabled for private deployments to avoid state pollution from peering partners. This prevents replies that have been SNATed by the partner and hairpin back on a different path.
- Workaround tested: allowlist the Kestrel source IPs in the conntrack prefilter and relax strict mode for the affected prefix. This preserved sessions during the window.

Recommended next steps:
- Rachel: request Kestrel to confirm whether they perform SNAT on egress to our peering, and if so provide the SNAT pool CIDRs.
- Jonas/Dev: evaluate automated route preference to keep reply path symmetric (BGP prepend or community policy to avoid hairpin).

I’ll attach the replay logs.

—Rishi

Mike —

Thanks for the dump. Two asks to unblock:
1) Please confirm whether your gateway is performing egress SNAT and, if yes, provide the SNAT pool ranges. If you can temporarily avoid SNAT for traffic destined to Redwood IP space, that will help determine if SNAT rewriting is the trigger.
2) Can you export a snapshot of the on-prem firewall state (or the SG rules) — we only need the rules and any NAT translations for the affected flows. A csv or screenshot is fine.

In parallel, we’ll:
- Apply a route preference to nudge return traffic back to our peering for the affected subnets (temporary mitigation).
- Put a short-term conntrack prefilter for Kestrel SNAT pool if provided.

If you’re available we can run a joint test at 11:00 PDT today.

—Rachel

Rachel / team —

We confirmed Kestrel does SNAT outbound to a 3-address pool for telemetry egress. I’ve attached the SG snapshot (sg-rules-snapshot-20271005.csv) and our NAT summary. We can avoid SNAT to Redwood prefixes for a short window. We’re good for the 11:00 PDT joint test.

Notes from our side:
- SNAT + hairpin via the partner path is the root cause — responses that come back with rewritten source IPs are not matched by connection tracking on your edge when the return takes a different upstream.
- We’ll coordinate an RFC to consider preserving original source for private peering or advertise SNAT pool to improve conntrack matching.

Thanks — looking forward to the joint run.

Mike Brown
Ops Lead, Kestrel IoT
